City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Agency, Community Development Financing Authority, Public Improvement Corporation, and Library Board of Trustees*
November 6, 2006
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, Community Development Agency, Community Development Financing Authority, Public Improvement Corporation, and Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor MacLean at 05:00 p.m. , on November 6, 2006, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on November 03, 2006, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

RECONVENE
Mayor MacLean reconvened the meeting at 6:02 p.m. All Council Members were present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that during a hearing on October 31, 2006, the court sustained a significant portion of the demurs to the extent that they dismissed the housing discrimination claim. The court directed a new briefing date so the action on the remainder of the complaint will move forward in January 2007.

Mayor MacLean recessed the meeting at 6:38 p.m. and reconvened at 6:46 p.m. All Council Members were present.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Roberta Ross, Dana Point: representing the League of Women Voters of Orange County, announced that the League will hold a public forum regarding the County’s harbors, beaches and parks, on Saturday, December 2, 2006, from 9:30 a.m. to noon, at the Irvine Ranch Water District, 15600 Sand Canyon, Irvine.
Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: expressed dissatisfaction with candidate’s campaign signs that attack opponents for City Council.
Haya Sakadjian, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the 108 members of the El Mirador Homeowners Association, expressed concern with the Mayor’s 2005 vote in support of a cell tower in their neighborhood.

21.
Concentration of Residential Community Care Facilities
Mayor MacLean announced that prior to tonight’s meeting, the City Council received 49 e-mails in favor of the recommended action and 25 names and signatures on a petition in favor of limiting these facilities.
The following expressed concern with the concentration of Residential Community Care Facilities in Aegean Hills and expressed support for the recommended action: Rob and Laine Teegarden, M.V.; Roberta L. Patton, M.V.; Joseph E. Kunsch, M.V.; Helen Workun, M.V.; Jerry Baglin, M.V.; Craig Macias, M.V.; Alexandra Cole, M.V.; and Elizabeth Yaeger, M.V.
The following presented written comments in favor of the recommended action: Scott Jameson, M.V.; Art and Joan Lucero, M.V.; Jim Brafford, M.V.; Thomas J. McHugh, M.V.; Robert A. Phillips, M.V.; Allen and Roberta Patton, M.V.; Fred and Phyllis Eisenbart, M.V.; Bangyi Yang and Mei Chang, M.V.; Reynaldo “Rey” De La Pena, M.V.; Robert and Shirley Greuel, M.V.; Verlanne Johnson, M.V.; Johnny, and Rachel Johnson and Becky Drake, M.V.; Jeanne Barrett, M.V.; Margaret Dimage, M.V.; Nola Ribbeck, M.V.; and Robert and Betty Wisniewski, M.V.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS
20.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended (AB 1234) (0480-70)
The City Council Members acknowledged the accuracy of their event and activities calendars as presented in the staff report.
COUNCIL MEMBER KELLEY
Expressed her gratitude to our country’s Veterans and reminded those who have served in the armed forces to display their medals on Veteran’s Day so members of the public can truly appreciate the sacrifices that our Veterans have made. Announced that the City will host a Veteran’s Day ceremony on Saturday, November 11, 2006, at 2:00 p.m. in the Kershaw Garden and encouraged families and children to stop by and help honor our Vets. Thanked the business partners that provide materials for the Community of Character program and stated that without their help, the City would not have such a successful program. Announced that the character word for the month of November is thankfulness, with a focus on our military men and women.
COUNCIL MEMBER LEDESMA
Thanked Council Member Kelley and Mayor MacLean for bringing two important issues to the City Council and thanked the residents who spoke on item 21 tonight.
COUNCIL MEMBER REAVIS
Encouraged residents to attend the Civic Light Opera at Saddleback College and discussed upcoming holiday programs, such as the Nutcracker. Reminded residents that we have many wonderful local businesses that give to the community and we should reward them by patronizing Mission Viejo stores and businesses. Announced that she has a few changes to her AB1234 report for the last Council Meeting and she will submit an updated copy to the City Clerk for the public record. Asked the City Manager to provide updates, at the next City Council Meeting, on the Ferrocarril landslide and on parking regulations at Newhart School . Stated that a large and respected business in Mission Viejo, Medix Ambulance, has been severely maligned and they were forced to defend themselves by mailing an open letter to the residents and publishing the same in the newspaper. Encouraged City Council candidates to remove their signs after tomorrow’s election.
MAYOR PRO TEMPORE URY
MAYOR MACLEAN
22.
An Ordinance Regulating the Use of Single Family Dwelling Structures; Local Regulation of Housing and State Preemptive Issues
Adam Probolsky, Apartment Association of Orange County: spoke in support of the recommended action and asked that the Council to include the Apartment Association in any meetings or discussions for their expertise and input.
Motion made by Mayor/Chair MacLean, seconded by Council Member/Agency Member Kelley, to approve and direct the City Attorney to review what other cities are doing and return to the City Council with more information and recommendations, and include the Apartment Association in discussions and meetings on this subject matter.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member/Agency Member Kelley, Council Member/Agency Member Ledesma, Council Member/Agency Member Reavis, Mayor Pro Tempore/Vice Chair Ury, and Mayor/Chair MacLean
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Reminded residents that tomorrow is election day and encouraged everyone to go out and exercise their civic duty. Expressed condolences to the family of deceased Laguna Hills Sheriff’s Deputy David Erickson and the family of Mission Viejo resident Neva Harris Whiles.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 8:00 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor MacLean adjourned the meeting in memory of Deputy David Erickson and Neva Harris Whiles, to November 15, 2006 at 6:00 p.m. for a Joint Workshop with the Planning and Transportation Commission Regarding the City’s Housing Element .
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of November 20, 2006
